annotation_description: Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon's second ability produces mana that can only be spent to cast Dragon or Omen spells. Sarkhan, Dragon Ascendant is a Human Druid, not a Dragon spell, so this restricted mana technically cannot be used to cast it. Colorless mana from option 1 could legally pay for the generic {1} in Sarkhan's cost.

Burst Lightning to face for 2 damage on an empty board wastes a flexible removal spell that could deal with future threats, while Sarkhan would develop a 2/2 body, create a Treasure token (by revealing a Dragon from hand), and accelerate toward casting powerful 4-drop Dragons.

Tapped Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon to float mana with nothing to spend it on in response to Burst Lightning. The mana will be wasted, and this unnecessarily taps a land that could potentially be useful later in the turn.

Failed to play Sunbillow Verge from hand before casting a spell (should always play land first when possible). Also, Clarion Conqueror (3/3 flyer that shuts down Hired Claw's pump ability) was likely a stronger play than Sarkhan, though Sarkhan + Treasure token provides ramp toward Magmatic Hellkite on turn 4.

Clarion Conqueror costs {2}{W} (3 mana), but the player only has 3 lands. They chose Clarion Conqueror over Sarkhan, Dragon Ascendant ({1}{R}, 2 mana). Sarkhan is the better play here for several reasons: (1) Sarkhan costs only 2 mana, leaving 1 mana open for Burst Lightning or the Hired Claw's pump ability response. (2) Sarkhan's ETB can behold a Dragon (revealing Magmatic Hellkite from hand) to create a Treasure token, which accelerates toward the 4-mana Magmatic Hellkite on turn 4. (3) Clarion Conqueror's static ability (shutting down activated abilities) has minimal impact against the opponent's current board - Hired Claw's pump ability requires the opponent to have lost life first, which hasn't happened yet. (4) Playing Sarkhan + having Burst Lightning open is much more flexible. The Treasure from Sarkhan would enable a turn 4 Magmatic Hellkite (which destroys the opponent's nonbasic land), a much more impactful curve.

Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon's second ability produces mana that can only be spent on Dragon spells or Omen spells. Sarkhan, Dragon Ascendant is a Human Druid creature, not a Dragon spell, so this restricted mana cannot legally be used to cast it. The colorless mana from option 1 would have been the correct choice to pay for the {1} generic portion of Sarkhan's {1}{R} cost.

Player declined to cast Burst Lightning at opponent's face during combat, missing 2 free damage. After combat, they could still play Mountain as their land drop and cast Emberheart Challenger (1R) using the two untapped lands, so the Burst Lightning wouldn't cost any tempo.

Casting Sarkhan, Dragon Ascendant on turn 4 with only 4 lands is questionable when the opponent has an Emberheart Challenger untapped that can trade with or attack into the 2/2 Sarkhan. More importantly, Sarkhan was cast using Cavern of Souls set to 'Ally' type, but Sarkhan is a Human Druid - not an Ally. The mana produced can only be spent on Ally creatures, so this appears to be a rules issue. Additionally, playing Sarkhan before combat means the opponent knows what they're facing. However, Sarkhan's behold ability can create a Treasure token (which helps ramp toward the expensive dragons in hand), so there is value in playing him pre-combat. The bigger concern is sequencing: Burst Lightning could target the Emberheart Challenger first to clear the way, and Clarion Conqueror at 3 mana with flying would be a stronger play that also shuts down activated abilities. Playing Sarkhan into an untapped 2/2 haste creature with prowess is risky.

Burst Lightning costs {R} and could remove the Emberheart Challenger (2/2) or Hired Claw (1/2) for just 1 mana, leaving 3 mana available. More importantly, casting Burst Lightning on Emberheart Challenger removes a prowess threat before it can grow, and the opponent's lands are all tapped so they can't respond. Additionally, Sarkhan costs {1}{R} and could be cast with the remaining mana after Burst Lightning, potentially setting up future Dragon synergy. Instead, MiniMx passed the entire turn doing nothing with 4 available mana, wasting a full turn of development.

MiniMx Heckler declined to use Burst Lightning on an attacking creature, with confused reasoning about declaring blockers despite having no creatures on the battlefield. Hired Claw is a persistent threat that deals incremental damage and can grow with +1/+1 counters. While the timing doesn't save damage this combat, removing it now prevents future value accumulation.

Hired Claw's attack trigger should have already dealt 1 damage to the opponent, enabling its {1}{R} activated ability to add a +1/+1 counter. The player has exactly {1}{R} available from untapped Sacred Foundry and Sunbillow Verge. Activating before combat damage would permanently grow Hired Claw to 2/3 and deal 1 extra combat damage, with the mana likely going unused otherwise.

MiniMx Heckler passed on using Burst Lightning during opponent's combat phase when enemy creatures (Hired Claw and Emberheart Challenger) were attacking. Hired Claw is a growing threat that deals incremental damage each time Lizards attack and can accumulate +1/+1 counters. Using Burst Lightning to remove it during combat would be mana-efficient since MiniMx Heckler had no other productive use for the mana this turn.

This is a permanent buff that costs only mana with no card investment, and the mana would otherwise go unused.
